When I hear people talk about prenatal testing and disabilities, I can’t help but think about my daughter, Vanessa.

Vanessa was born with spina bifida and hydrocephalus. There have been challenges, surgeries, appointments, and worries along the way. But there has also been laughter, courage, determination, and a love so deep that it has changed my life forever.

Vanessa is not a diagnosis. She is not a medical chart or a test result. She is my daughter. She has taught me patience, strength, gratitude, and what unconditional love truly means.

One of my favorite things is seeing the simple joys that make her smile. She absolutely loves listening to Layla 💕🐱 and following Laylathaplaya. Seeing her light up when she watches and listens is a reminder that happiness is often found in the little things.

If I could go back and choose my life again, I would choose her every single time.

Children with disabilities are not glitches. They are human beings with personalities, dreams, feelings, and an incredible ability to touch the lives of everyone around them.

I am proud to be Vanessa’s mom, and my life is better because she is in it. 🎗️💛🐈‍⬛
Is all human life sacred? Or just the right ones that are important every election cycle? I ask this of both parties

Children are a gift from the Lord; they are a reward from him. Psalms 127:3. SILENCE HAS A VOICE!
We are not only held accountable for our words according to scripture, we are also held accountable for our silence. When we say nothing, then what people have done is approved. When silence is the response to someone's actions, we have endorsed them. To choose to speak out when something is said and done that is not right will take courage. Silence is the easy way to respond, because it has lied to us that saying nothing keeps peace.
We stay silent so we don't lose friends, a job, or even followers.
To not speak for the unborn lives, that society has determined it is not a life, is accepting their sins!
